newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan power plant to offer shares to public.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan power plant to offer shares to public.

text.p: Pakistan's private Japan Power Generation Ltd will issue 13.8 million 10-rupee shares to the public later this month, a company director said on Tuesday.
Asad Ali Uppal told Reuters the state Corporate Law Authority (CLA) had approved the offering at the weekend.

Japan Power will publish its prospectus on Wednesday and is likely to float 138 million rupees ($3.73 million) worth of shares on October 17 or 21 pending CLA approval of the subscription date, he said.

Uppal said the firm had placed 135 million rupees worth of shares with individuals, firms and associates in July, while shares worth $25 million had been placed abroad in March through the Bahrain-based Islamic Investment Company of the Gulf.

Japan Power successfully secured finance for the $123 million project in September 1995. The plant, which will have a capacity of 120 megawatts, is located at Raiwand, near Lahore, and due to come onstream in March 1997.
The state-owned Water and Power Development Authority will buy the electricity it generates at 6.5 U.S. cents per kilowatt hour under an agreement signed in March 1995.
Japan Power has agreements with Toyota Tsusho Corp of Japan for a supplier credit of $82 million.
